Four-Cycle Engine Theory Section 3: Four-Cycle Engine Theory Introduction Four events must occur in the correct sequence and at the correct time for the engine to run correctly. These events are (A) intake, (B) compression, (C) power, and (D) exhaust. (A) Intake (C) Power 001684 The piston is traveling from top dead center (TDC) to bottom dead center (BDC). The cam has opened the intake valve. The piston's downward movement in the cylinder creates a partial vacuum in the cylinder. Air at atmospheric pressure is drawn into the cylinder through the airbox and is mixed with fuel, supplied by the injector, as it enters the cylinder. The intake stroke is complete when the piston reaches BDC. (B) Compression 001686 Combustion is already in progress when the piston reaches TDC. The intake and exhaust valves remain closed as expanding gases of combustion force the piston downward. (D) Exhaust 001687 The exhaust stroke begins when the piston has reached BDC and has started its upward movement. The intake valve is closed, and the exhaust valve is open to let gases escape. 001685 As the piston reaches BDC, both the intake and exhaust valves are closed. The piston moves upward toward TDC and the fuel-air mixture is compressed. Ignition occurs just before the piston reaches TDC. 817cc Engine Service Manual Service Manual 13

Systematic Inspection If engine will not start and the cause of malfunction is not readily apparent, perform a systematic inspection in the following order: 1. Fuel 2. Ignition 3. Compression This inspection, performed in a systematic manner, can usually be done in a matter of minutes. It is the quickest 817cc Engine Service Manual Service Manual

Checking Fuel Pressure • NG: 3.5 – 7.0 in H2O (0.87 – 1.74 kPa) • LP: 10 – 12 in H2O (2.49 – 2.99 kPa) For gaseous units, check the following: • Is there sufficient fuel supply from the meter? • Is the fuel supply pipe the correct size? • Are there any bends or kinks in the flexible supply line? Checking Ignition See Section 7: Ignition for testing procedures. Checking Oil Pressure Proceed as follows to check oil pressure: 1. Remove generator or engine from service. 2. Inspect engine crankcase oil level. If necessary, add the recommended oil to the dipstick FULL mark. DO NOT OVERFILL. 3. See Figure 4-6. Remove oil pressure switch and install an oil pressure gauge using a tee and pipe nipple between the block and original pressure gauge. Figure 4-6. A 020825 Figure 4-6. Remove Pressure Sensor 4. Thoroughly clean unit to remove any spilled oil. 5. Start engine while observing the oil pressure reading on the gauge. Oil pressure should be 1550 psi (103-345 kPa) at 70 °F (21 °C). NOTE: A pressure relief valve limits the maximum pressure in the system to 30-40 psi (206-276 kPa). 6. Shut down engine. 7. Install original pressure sensor into sensor location on unit. 817cc Engine Service Manual Service Manual General Information 8. Clean area to remove any residual oil left from performing the test. 9. Put generator/engine back into service. 10. Run engine and verify there are no leaks. Checking Compression Proceed as follows to check engine compression: 1. Disconnect the ECM. 2. Manually open throttle plate on the ETC to wide open throttle (WOT) position. 3. Connect a remote button starter switch from the battery positive to the starter relay. 4. Remove both spark plugs and insert a compression gauge (Generac P/N GN04001) into either cylinder (one cylinder at a time). 5. Turn engine over with engine starter until there is no further increase in pressure. Record this reading. 6. Repeat procedure on other cylinder and record reading. The compression difference between both cylinders should not exceed 25%. More than 25% indicates loss of compression in the cylinder with lower pressure. To calculate the difference in percentage, divide the difference in PSI (kPa) by the higher pressure reading. See examples below. Engine #3: (48 psi ÷ 160 psi) [330.9 kPa ÷ 1,103.1 kPa] = 0.30 = 30% difference Using this method of calculation, Cylinder 2 in Engine #3 has lost significant compression. Ignition Section 7: Ignition Ignition Check The ignition system is controlled by the ECM. The coils are powered by the IR and fuse F4. The IR is controlled by the ECM. In order to generate a fault code, the following conditions may apply: • The ECM will check if ignition coil current is above the threshold when coil is firing. • The ECM will check if ignition coil current is below the threshold when the coil is firing. • The ECM will check if ignition coil current is detected when coil is not firing. Check Valve Springs 004442 Gasket Removal Verify sealing surface is completely clean and free of old gasket material before installing a new gasket. Residual gasket material or dirt can prevent the new gasket from sealing completely. An incorrectly sealed gasket may cause the engine to leak oil, lose compression, or overheat. 41

Cylinder Head and Valves It is critical to completely remove old gasket material without damaging sealing surfaces. Aluminum is very soft and easy to scratch and gouge. A new gasket may not seal completely if the underlying surface is damaged. Generac does not recommend using a wire brush or abrasive sanding to remove gaskets. Use a metal gasket scraper specifically designed for this purpose. Scrape gasket at a shallow angle—almost parallel to the sealing surface. Wipe sealing surface with a clean, dry, lint-free rag after removing gasket residue. If the gasket is difficult to scrape off, spray it with an aerosol gasket removal compound. Allow the compound to soak into the gasket for the length of time recommended by the manufacturer (typically 10– 20 minutes), then use the gasket scraper again. NOTE: Some gasket removal compounds contain chemicals damaging to plastics. Read and follow the directions on the product label before use. Section 10: Electric Starter Electric Starter General Information See Figure 10-1. The starter motor utilizes a solenoid, similar to an automobile starter, to assist in pinion gear engagement. When the starter motor is activated, the pinion gear engages a ring gear attached to the engine flywheel and cranks the engine. Figure 10-1. Figure 10-1. Starter Motor 009583 Troubleshooting IMPORTANT NOTE: Do not rotate engine with electric starter while spark plugs are removed, unless using a compression gauge. Arcing at the spark plug ends may ignite fuel vapor exiting the spark plug hole. NOTE: If a starting problem is encountered, inspect the engine thoroughly to eliminate it as the cause of starting difficulty. Check engine for free rotation by removing spark plugs and flywheel guard and turning the crankshaft with a socket and ratchet or breaker bar. Verify it rotates freely. Engine cranks slowly: • Additional drag on engine, affecting starter performance (see note above). • Discharged battery. • Faulty electrical connection (battery circuit). • Dirty or worn starter motor commutator, bearing, weak magnets, worn brushes, etc. • Incorrect oil viscosity for temperature expected. • Battery leads too long or wire too small. • Underpowered battery. Engine will not crank if: • Faulty safety interlocks. • Discharged battery. • Faulty electrical connections. • Faulty starter motor switch (open circuit). • Open circuit in starter motor. 817cc Engine Service Manual Service Manual • Brushes sticking, etc. • Faulty solenoid. Starter motor spins but does not crank engine: • Sticking pinion gear due to dirt. • Damaged pinion or ring gear. • Damaged or faulty battery. • Incorrect rotation due to reversed motor polarity. • all motors rotate counterclockwise viewed from pinion gear. • Damaged solenoid. Starter motor spins but will not stop: • Faulty starter switch. • Solenoid stuck engaged. Test Equipment Digital Multimeter (DMM) See Figure 10-2. Section 11: Lubrication System Lubrication System Description The Generac 817CC G26 G-Force V-Twin engine uses a full pressure lubrication system with an oil filter. A gerotor oil pump draws oil from a screened oil pickup in the sump and pumps oil through the oil filter. Filtered oil flows through an oil gallery in the sump and is distributed to the main bearings, connecting rod bearings, hydraulic lash adjusters, and camshaft bearings. Engine oil pressure varies with oil viscosity, ambient air temperature differences, operating temperatures, and engine load. • Oil pressure - @ 70 °F (21 °C): 15 – 50 psi (103 – 345 kPa) NOTE: A pressure relief valve limits the maximum oil pressure in the system to 30 – 40 psi (206 – 276 kPa). Protection Systems Low Oil Pressure Switch See Figure 11-1. The engine is usually equipped with a normally open type, low oil pressure switch (A) which closes the circuit between the terminals when oil pressure drops below 10 +/- 3 psi (69 kPa). The engine will shut down on low oil pressure if one terminal is connected to the ignition ground wire and the other terminal is connected to ground. The low oil pressure switch can also be connected to an alarm or light to indicate low oil pressure, instead of shutting down the engine. Figure 11-1. A 020543 Figure 11-1. Low Oil Pressure Switch A delay built into the shutdown system on some engine applications allows oil pressure to build during starting. The delay allows the engine to run for about 10 seconds before sensing oil pressure. The engine shuts down if the engine is wired for low oil pressure shutdown and the system senses low oil pressure during operation. The 817cc Engine Service Manual Service Manual engine will not run until 8 psi (55 kPa) of oil pressure is reached. If a restart is attempted within five seconds after shutdown, the engine may NOT start. The system needs 10 seconds to reset. Checking Engine Oil Level CAUTION Engine damage.
